_comment: Filled in as scenarios are actually implemented, not ahead of reality — see docs/scenarios/ for what's actually built.

components.name: k6 (load test)
components.description: Traffic generator started from the control panel - not part of the deployed stack, only exists while a scenario is running

details.purpose: One-off container per run (see the traffic panel); hits the same external entry point (nginx) real clients would

components.name: nginx
components.description: External entry point for LinkApi and RedirectApi - the only reason either can have more than one replica

details.purpose: Reverse proxy in front of link-api/redirect-api; re-resolves their service name against Docker's embedded DNS on a short TTL so it picks up replicas added/removed via Scale without a config reload

components.name: Frontend App
components.description: Demo UI — register/login, create a short link, visit it

details.purpose: The only thing an actual person interacts with in this whole stack
Owns users_db (the only writer to it, and the only one that migrates it)

components.name: LinkApi
components.description: Creates short links (hash generated here), reads them back through a cache

details.purpose: POST /links generates the hash, optionally attaches userId from a Bearer token (no [Authorize] — anonymous still works), and publishes it; GET /links/{hash} is a cached read against links_db

components.name: RedirectApi
components.description: Resolves a short link, issues a 302, and records the click

details.purpose: Cache-first read of links_db (same data LinkApi writes); 404 on unknown hash; publishes ClickTrackedEvent right before redirecting

components.name: RabbitMQ
components.description: Durable queue between the two APIs and their workers

details.purpose: Decouples each API's synchronous response from the actual Postgres write it triggers
details.topology: topic exchange "events"; queue "shortener-service.link-created" bound to routing key "link.created", queue "traffic-service.click-tracked" bound to "click.tracked" — both declared by the app itself, not a static definitions.json

links.config: sandbox/infra/rabbitmq/definitions.json (unused placeholder, see its own comment)

details.purpose: Owns links_db (the only writer, and the only one that migrates it); redelivery-safe (skips if the hash is already stored)
Owns clicks_db (the only writer, and the only one that migrates it); redelivery-safe (skips if the event's Id is already stored)

components.name: PgCat
components.description: Connection pooler in front of Postgres - every service talks to pgcat, never to postgres directly

details.purpose: One pool per physical database (users_db/links_db/clicks_db), each a single unsharded shard for now; multiplexes many short-lived app connections onto a small server-side pool per database

components.name: Redis
components.description: Cache of hash → link, shared key format between LinkApi and RedirectApi

details.purpose: Cache-aside: read-through on miss, populated by whichever service reads or creates first

components.name: users_db
components.description: Own physical database, not just a schema — real isolation from links_db/clicks_db

components.name: links_db
components.description: Own physical database — target design shards this one (scenario 4)

details.purpose: Links(hash PK, originalLink, shortenLink, createdAt, userId?)

connections.label: Create / look up / visit a link
Generated load
connections.notes: Only present while a scenario is running from the traffic panel.

connections.label: Proxy: create / look up a link
Read on cache miss
connections.format: read-only from this service — ShortenerService owns writes/migrations

connections.label: Publish LinkCreatedEvent
connections.format: { hash, originalLink, shortenLink, createdAt, userId? } → JSON, routing key "link.created"
connections.notes: Falls back to a local SQLite queue if the broker is unreachable; retried every 30s.

connections.label: Read on cache miss
connections.format: read-only from this service — ShortenerService owns writes/migrations

connections.label: Publish ClickTrackedEvent
connections.format: { id, hash, inboundLink, outboundLink, clickedAt } → JSON, routing key "click.tracked"
connections.notes: Published right before the 302 response; falls back to the same SQLite-queue pattern as LinkApi if the broker is unreachable. A 404 never publishes anything.

connections.label: Pooled connection
connections.format: pool_mode = transaction, 1 unsharded shard - see scenario 4 for sharding this one

scenarios.name: Minimal stack
scenarios.description: Register/login, create a short link, resolve it. RabbitMQ already decouples the write; no sharding or replicas yet.
scenarios.focus: Cache-aside reads, eventual consistency on the write path, connection pooling patterns (AddDbContextPool vs AddPooledDbContextFactory), database-per-service isolation

scenarios.name: Click tracking (async)
scenarios.description: Visiting a link publishes a second event; TrafficService persists it independently of the redirect itself.
scenarios.focus: A second, symmetric async write path; JWT userId flows into the first path (LinkApi validates optionally, no [Authorize])
